title: Understanding the teenage brain, with Eva Telzer, PhD

sentences.en: There may be no stage in life that's more maligned than adolescence.
sentences.zh: 人生中恐怕没有哪个阶段比青春期更受诟病了。

sentences.en: When people think of teenagers, the words that may come to mind include moody, impulsive, risk-taking, and self-centered.
sentences.zh: 提到青少年，人们脑海中浮现的词汇往往包括：喜怒无常、冲动、爱冒险和以自我为中心。

sentences.en: In the movies, on TV, and in our imaginations, teenagers drive too fast, they experiment with drugs and alcohol, and they cave to peer pressure to take other unwise risks.
sentences.zh: 在电影、电视和我们的想象中，青少年总是开车超速、尝试烟酒，并屈从于同伴压力去冒其他不必要的风险。

sentences.en: Looking back, many of us probably remember doing a few of those things ourselves when we were teens.
sentences.zh: 回首往事，我们很多人可能都记得自己在十几岁时也做过其中的几件事。

sentences.en: And teenage brains, so the stereotype goes, are driving these actions.
sentences.zh: 按照刻板印象，正是青少年时期的大脑在驱动这些行为。

sentences.en: These brains just haven't developed enough for young people to make good decisions.
sentences.zh: 这种观点认为，年轻人的大脑发育尚不成熟，无法做出明智的决定。

sentences.en: But researchers are increasingly finding that this negative view of the adolescent brain is inaccurate and incomplete.
sentences.zh: 但研究人员正越来越多地发现，这种对青少年大脑的负面看法既不准确也不全面。

sentences.en: Yes, teenagers are still a work in progress, but the brain changes that mark adolescents make it a time of great opportunity and growth, as well as risk.
sentences.zh: 没错，青少年确实处于成长过程中，但标志着青春期的大脑变化，使其成为一个充满巨大机遇和成长空间，同时也伴随着风险的时期。

sentences.en: So what is happening in the teenage brain?
sentences.zh: 那么，青少年大脑中究竟发生了什么？

sentences.en: Do adolescents take more risks than other age groups, and is that risk-taking always bad?
sentences.zh: 青少年是否比其他年龄段的人更爱冒险？这种冒险行为总是坏事吗？

sentences.en: Who has more influence over teens' behavior, their parents or their peers?
sentences.zh: 谁对青少年的行为影响更大：父母还是同伴？

sentences.en: Are teens really more self-centered than adults?
sentences.zh: 青少年真的比成年人更以自我为中心吗？

sentences.en: And how might social media and other technology use be changing teens' behavior and development?
sentences.zh: 社交媒体和其他科技的使用又是如何改变青少年的行为和发展的？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Eva Telzer, an associate professor of psychology and neuroscience at the University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill.
sentences.zh: 今天的嘉宾是北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校的心理学与神经科学副教授伊娃·特尔泽博士。

sentences.en: She studies teens' brain development and behavior, with a focus on risk-taking, family and peer relationships, pro-social behavior, and long-term psychological well-being.
sentences.zh: 她研究青少年的大脑发育和行为，重点关注冒险行为、家庭与同伴关系、亲社会行为以及长期的心理健康。

sentences.en: She's also interested in how social media and technology are affecting teens' brain development.
sentences.zh: 她还对社交媒体和科技如何影响青少年的大脑发育很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And she is the co-director of the Winston National Center on Technology Use, Brain, and Psychological Development.
sentences.zh: 她同时也是温斯顿国家科技使用、大脑与心理发展中心的主任之一。

sentences.en: She's received many awards for her work, including APA's Boyd-McCandless Award for Early Career Contributions
sentences.zh: 她因其研究工作获得了许多奖项，包括美国心理学会颁发的博伊德-麦坎德利斯早期职业贡献奖，

sentences.en: to Developmental Psychology, and the association's Distinguished Scientific Award for Early Career Contributions to Psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及该协会颁发的杰出科学早期职业贡献奖。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. Telzer.
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天参加我们的节目，特尔泽博士。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Let's start with a definition so that we're on the same page in terms of what age group we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我们先从定义开始，以便我们对所讨论的年龄段达成共识。

sentences.en: In your research, how do you define adolescence?
sentences.zh: 在您的研究中，您是如何定义青春期的？

sentences.en: Is it just the teenage years from 13 to 19, or does it encompass a broader range?
sentences.zh: 它仅仅是指13到19岁的青少年时期，还是涵盖了更广的范围？

sentences.en: So, defining adolescence is quite complicated.
sentences.zh: 定义青春期其实相当复杂。

sentences.en: It is not necessarily defined by age.
sentences.zh: 它并不一定由年龄来界定。

sentences.en: It's not necessarily defined by other markers, such as the onset and offset of puberty.
sentences.zh: 它也不一定由其他标志（如青春期的开始和结束）来界定。

sentences.en: And so, when we study adolescence, we often are following youth across time to look at change.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们研究青春期时，我们通常会长期追踪年轻人以观察其变化。

sentences.en: And we typically start in middle school, so 6th and 7th graders in the United States, for example,
sentences.zh: 我们通常从初中开始，例如在美国，从六年级和七年级学生开始，

sentences.en: and following them through the end of high school, so 12th grade in the United States.
sentences.zh: 一直追踪到高中结束，也就是美国的十二年级。

sentences.en: Sometimes our research starts a little bit younger and sometimes goes a little bit older.
sentences.zh: 有时我们的研究开始得早一点，有时结束得晚一点。

sentences.en: But for the most part, we're studying adolescence from approximately 6th grade to 12th grade.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，我们研究的青春期大约是从六年级到十二年级。

sentences.en: So, one of the most common negative stereotypes about teens is that they take a lot of unnecessary and unwise risks, and that this risk-taking tendency is wired into their brains.
sentences.zh: 关于青少年最常见的负面刻板印象之一是他们会进行大量不必要且不明智的冒险，而且这种冒险倾向是刻在他们大脑里的。

sentences.en: How accurate is that?
sentences.zh: 这种说法有多准确？

sentences.en: Are teens more prone to take risks compared with adults and even younger children?
sentences.zh: 与成年人甚至更小的孩子相比，青少年真的更容易冒险吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so there's a fair amount of research looking at risk-taking behaviors and how this might change across development.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实有相当多的研究在观察冒险行为以及它如何随发育而变化。

sentences.en: So, following youth starting in childhood through adolescence to adulthood, and even doing this
sentences.zh: 通过追踪年轻人从童年、青春期到成年期的过程，甚至进行跨国研究，

sentences.en: work across nationally, researchers have found what looks like an inverted U-shaped pattern with adolescents showing the highest levels of risk-taking behaviors.
sentences.zh: 研究人员发现了一种类似倒U型的模式，其中青少年表现出的冒险行为水平最高。

sentences.en: So, this ranges from behaviors that might be construed as negative, like substance use behaviors, but also less risky behaviors.
sentences.zh: 这涵盖了可能被视为负面的行为，比如物质滥用，但也包括一些风险较低的行为。

sentences.en: So, on an experimental task, for example, where you can manipulate rewards that they might receive,
sentences.zh: 例如，在一项实验任务中，你可以操纵他们可能获得的奖励，

sentences.en: but a risk of not getting that reward, we can see that adolescents more so than children and more so than adults choose to take the risk in order to receive that reward.
sentences.zh: 但如果存在得不到奖励的风险，我们可以看到青少年比儿童和成年人更愿意为了获得奖励而冒险。

sentences.en: And this is thought to be driven by sensation-seeking and reward-seeking behaviors that are substantiated in the brain.
sentences.zh: 这被认为是由大脑中得到证实的寻求刺激和寻求奖励的行为所驱动的。

sentences.en: So, there's quite a bit of research out there showing that an area of the brain called the
sentences.zh: 因此，有相当多的研究表明，大脑中一个被称为

sentences.en: ventral striatum, which codes for reward value, is more activated in adolescents when they receive
sentences.zh: 腹侧纹状体的区域（它负责编码奖励价值）在青少年获得

sentences.en: rewards and when they take risks, then this brain region is activated in children or adults.
sentences.zh: 奖励和冒险时，比在儿童或成年人身上表现出更强的激活。

sentences.en: So, it is true based on the empirical research out there that adolescents are more likely to take
sentences.zh: 所以，根据现有的实证研究，青少年确实更有可能

sentences.en: risks and that there is evidence from the brain that supports why this might be happening.
sentences.zh: 冒险，而且大脑中也有证据支持这种现象发生的原因。

sentences.en: So, it's perhaps driven by this tendency to seek out rewards, but the widely held stereotype that this
sentences.zh: 这或许是由这种寻求奖励的倾向所驱动的，但那种认为这

sentences.en: is very negative and drives only negative behaviors like teens recklessly driving or jumping off a bridge
sentences.zh: 非常负面，只会导致青少年鲁莽驾驶、跳桥

sentences.en: or doing other more negative risks may be overstated because teens are engaging in so many positive risks
sentences.zh: 或进行其他负面冒险行为的普遍刻板印象可能被夸大了，因为青少年也参与了许多积极的冒险，

sentences.en: that are sometimes overlooked in the media as well as parents' worries about what teens might be doing with their peers, for example.
sentences.zh: 这些冒险有时被媒体以及父母对青少年与同伴交往的担忧所忽视。

sentences.en: And so, there's lots of risks that might be construed as more positive.
sentences.zh: 所以，有很多风险其实可以被解读为更积极的。

sentences.en: So, for example, if you're in a class and the teacher raises a question, some teens may feel very nervous about raising their hand and answering the question.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，如果你在课堂上，老师提出了一个问题，有些青少年可能会因为举手回答问题而感到非常紧张。

sentences.en: But you might do so.
sentences.zh: 但你可能会这样做。

sentences.en: You might raise your hand and answer the question even if you're kind of afraid of your peers thinking poorly of you or you're not getting the answer right.
sentences.zh: 你可能会举手回答问题，即使你有点担心同伴会怎么看你，或者担心自己答错。

sentences.en: And so, that's just one example of a positive risk.
sentences.zh: 这只是积极冒险的一个例子。

sentences.en: There's also what we define as a pro-social risk.
sentences.zh: 还有一种我们定义为“亲社会冒险”的行为。

sentences.en: So, this is going out of your way, potentially risking social status or other types of risks that may come with some backlash in order to help somebody else.
sentences.zh: 这指的是为了帮助他人，不惜冒着损害社会地位或其他可能招致反弹的风险。

sentences.en: So, as an example, there might be a kid getting bullied in school.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，学校里可能有孩子被欺负。

sentences.en: And so, a pro-social risk would be standing up to the bully and helping out that kid who's being bullied.
sentences.zh: 那么，亲社会冒险就是站出来对抗欺凌者，帮助那个被欺负的孩子。

sentences.en: And so, there's this potentially huge risk that the bully is going to backlash at you or that your social status may be viewed more negatively by some of the cool kids in school.
sentences.zh: 这其中存在巨大的潜在风险，比如欺凌者可能会报复你，或者你在学校里那些“酷孩子”眼中的社会地位可能会变差。

sentences.en: But the potential positive of this is helping out that kid who might be getting bullied.
sentences.zh: 但这样做的潜在积极意义是帮助了那个可能正在被欺负的孩子。

sentences.en: So, you mentioned an area of the brain that's activated, right, which is why some teens may be taking risks.
sentences.zh: 你提到了大脑中有一个区域会被激活，这解释了为什么有些青少年会冒险。

sentences.en: Does the same thing happen in adults?
sentences.zh: 成年人身上也会发生同样的情况吗？

sentences.en: And how is it that adults can regulate that?
sentences.zh: 成年人又是如何调节这种行为的呢？

sentences.en: So, there is heightened ventral stride and activation in adults, too, when they engage in risks and receive rewards.
sentences.zh: 成年人在进行冒险和获得奖励时，腹侧纹状体也会有高度激活。

sentences.en: It's just not as high as it is in adolescents.
sentences.zh: 只是没有青少年那么高。

sentences.en: So, there's thought to be less of this reward drive in adults.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们认为成年人对奖励的驱动力相对较小。

sentences.en: There's what is now thought to be a relatively simplified view of the development of reward-seeking and risk-taking behavior, which is not necessarily robustly
sentences.zh: 目前有一种关于寻求奖励和冒险行为发展的相对简化的观点，这种观点在研究中

sentences.en: supported in the research, which I think you're alluding to, which is this idea of regulation,
sentences.zh: 并不一定得到强有力的支持，我想你指的就是这种调节的概念，

sentences.en: where adults are better regulated, have a more developed prefrontal cortex, and therefore, they can down-regulate that ventral stride and response.
sentences.zh: 即成年人的调节能力更好，拥有更发达的前额叶皮层，因此他们可以下调腹侧纹状体的反应。

sentences.en: But that's not necessarily the full story here.
sentences.zh: 但这并不一定是事情的全部。

sentences.en: Adolescents actually are very good at regulating their behavior.
sentences.zh: 青少年实际上非常擅长调节自己的行为。

sentences.en: They have not a broken brain or undeveloped prefrontal cortex, but a regulatory system that's very flexible and can be engaged to meet their motivational goals.
sentences.zh: 他们的大脑并没有受损，前额叶皮层也没有发育不全，而是拥有一个非常灵活的调节系统，可以根据他们的动机目标进行调整。

sentences.en: And so, it's not that they can't regulate their behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以，并不是他们无法调节自己的行为。

sentences.en: It's just that sometimes their goal is not to regulate their behavior because the reward of one behavior just may be much more highly valued than the reward of
sentences.zh: 只是有时他们的目标不是调节行为，因为某种行为带来的奖励可能比

sentences.en: regulating that behavior.
sentences.zh: 调节行为本身所带来的奖励价值更高。

sentences.en: And so, they choose to engage in it.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们选择了去参与。

sentences.en: It's not that they are incapable of not stopping themselves from engaging in it.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说他们无法阻止自己去参与。

sentences.en: There's an idea that teenagers are egged on by their peers to take risks and that their parents don't have a whole lot of influence over them at this point in life.
sentences.zh: 有一种观点认为，青少年是在同伴的怂恿下冒险的，而父母在这一人生阶段对他们几乎没有影响力。

sentences.en: What have you found in your research?
sentences.zh: 您在研究中发现了什么？

sentences.en: Do parents or peers have more influence when it comes to teens' risk-taking?
sentences.zh: 在青少年冒险方面，父母还是同伴的影响力更大？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, there is absolutely this stereotype out there that peers are going to drive adolescents to engage in largely negative behaviors and that parents have
sentences.zh: 绝对存在这样一种刻板印象，即同伴会驱使青少年参与主要是负面的行为，而父母在

sentences.en: less of a role in affecting their teens' decision-making.
sentences.zh: 影响青少年决策方面的作用较小。

sentences.en: And what's remarkable is that there's really been no research to support this and not a lot of research out there has even been done to ask this very question.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，实际上并没有研究支持这一点，甚至很少有研究去探讨这个问题。

sentences.en: And so, we have completed several studies now in my lab to look at the relative role of parent and peer influence on adolescents' risk-taking behaviors as well as their more
sentences.zh: 因此，我的实验室现在已经完成了几项研究，来观察父母和同伴对青少年冒险行为以及

sentences.en: positive types of behaviors like pro-social behaviors or healthy behaviors.
sentences.zh: 更积极的行为（如亲社会行为或健康行为）的相对影响。

sentences.en: And what we have found is across multiple studies now, either parents and peers have a similar influence on adolescents'
sentences.zh: 我们通过多项研究发现，父母和同伴对青少年

sentences.en: decision-making or parents actually outweigh that of their peers.
sentences.zh: 决策的影响力要么相当，要么父母的影响力实际上超过了同伴。

sentences.en: In one study, for example, adolescents have the decision to take a risk or not in the presence of conflicting information from their parent and their peers.
sentences.zh: 例如，在一项研究中，青少年需要在父母和同伴意见冲突的情况下决定是否冒险。

sentences.en: So, their parent may have said, take the risk and their peer may have said, no, play it safe and vice versa.
sentences.zh: 父母可能说“去冒险”，而同伴可能说“不，稳妥点”，反之亦然。

sentences.en: And what we find is that teens are more likely to go along with what their parent says than with what their peer says in this risk-taking context.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在这种冒险情境下，青少年更有可能听从父母的建议，而不是同伴的。

sentences.en: In other studies, for example, looking at their risk attitudes and their pro-social attitudes, we find that teens go along
sentences.zh: 在其他研究中，例如观察他们的风险态度和亲社会态度时，我们发现青少年在

sentences.en: with their parents' attitudes and their peers' attitudes at about a 50-50 level.
sentences.zh: 听从父母态度和同伴态度方面大约是五五开。

sentences.en: So, they're just as likely to follow what their parents' attitudes are as they are to follow what their peers' attitudes are.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他们追随父母态度的可能性与追随同伴态度的可能性是一样的。

sentences.en: And what's actually quite striking is that they stick with their own attitudes more often than they go along with what their parents or their peers think.
sentences.zh: 而且非常引人注目的是，他们坚持自己态度的频率，比听从父母或同伴想法的频率更高。

sentences.en: And so, rather than being like overly susceptible to what other people think in their social environment, especially their peers, adolescents are actually kind of sticking
sentences.zh: 因此，青少年并非像刻板印象中那样容易受到社会环境中其他人（尤其是同伴）的影响，他们实际上

sentences.en: to their guns more often than they are to follow what their peers think or even what their parents think.
sentences.zh: 更多时候是在坚持自己的立场，而不是盲从同伴甚至父母的想法。

sentences.en: And we think that this is quite remarkable compared to the overall stereotype that teens are overly susceptible to others.
sentences.zh: 与青少年容易受他人影响的普遍刻板印象相比，我们认为这一发现非常了不起。

sentences.en: And actually, teens kind of are independent thinkers and stick with what they think are positive and negative behaviors more so than they are to go along with others.
sentences.zh: 实际上，青少年更像是独立的思考者，他们坚持自己认为积极或消极的行为，而不是随波逐流。

sentences.en: You found that risk-taking can be adaptive in development.
sentences.zh: 您发现冒险在发展过程中具有适应性。

sentences.en: I mean, what do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，您所说的“适应性”是指什么？

sentences.en: How does risk-taking essentially help young people grow and develop?
sentences.zh: 冒险行为本质上是如何帮助年轻人成长和发展的？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So, there's lots of different ways that risk-taking can be adaptive.
sentences.zh: 冒险行为在很多方面都可以是适应性的。

sentences.en: One is that just from an evolutionary perspective, going out, learning from your environment,
sentences.zh: 首先，从进化角度来看，走出去、从环境中学习、

sentences.en: engaging in kind of flexible behaviors, trial and error helps adolescents to learn and develop and explore who they are and what matters to them.
sentences.zh: 参与灵活的行为、通过试错，有助于青少年学习、发展并探索他们是谁以及什么对他们重要。

sentences.en: It allows them to make new friends, to get away from the family and find a mate.
sentences.zh: 这使他们能够结交新朋友，脱离家庭并寻找伴侣。

sentences.en: So, sort of from that kind of evolutionary perspective, it promotes development.
sentences.zh: 所以，从进化角度来看，它促进了发展。

sentences.en: There's also adaptive ways that it can happen just in terms of these more positive risks that I alluded to earlier, raising your hand in class or asking your crush out on a date
sentences.zh: 此外，正如我之前提到的，在更积极的冒险方面，它也有适应性，比如在课堂上举手、约心仪的对象出去约会，

sentences.en: or trying out for a challenging sports activity or something else that might be challenging that you might
sentences.zh: 或者尝试一项具有挑战性的体育活动，或者其他你可能

sentences.en: be scared to do but kind of taking the risk to try it are all ways that risks can be highly adaptive in adolescence.
sentences.zh: 感到害怕但仍愿意冒险去尝试的事情，这些都是冒险在青春期具有高度适应性的方式。

sentences.en: Now, you've tackled another stereotype in your research, which is that teens are more self-centered than adults.
sentences.zh: 您在研究中还打破了另一个刻板印象，即青少年比成年人更以自我为中心。

sentences.en: That's a pretty common idea.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常普遍的观点。

sentences.en: But as you've pointed out, there's a countervailing stereotype that many teens are driven to change the world for the better.
sentences.zh: 但正如您所指出的，还有一种相反的刻板印象，即许多青少年有动力去改变世界，使其变得更美好。

sentences.en: I mean, a lot of the big social movements of our time from climate change to Black Lives Matter have been led in part by adolescence.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们这个时代许多重大的社会运动，从气候变化到“黑人的命也是命”，在一定程度上都是由青少年领导的。

sentences.en: So, how do these ideas fit together?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些观点是如何统一起来的呢？

sentences.en: Are teens more self-centered than adults or are they more idealistic and driven to do more good in the world?
sentences.zh: 青少年真的比成年人更以自我为中心吗？还是说他们更理想主义，更有动力为世界做更多好事？

sentences.en: Adolescence, I think, is just such a remarkable developmental period.
sentences.zh: 我认为青春期是一个非常了不起的发展阶段。

sentences.en: So, for all of the reasons that the brain is developing and changing and thought to be negative are many of the reasons that adolescents are engaging in really positive behavior.
sentences.zh: 大脑发育、变化以及被认为负面的所有原因，往往也是青少年参与真正积极行为的原因。

sentences.en: So, for example, increases in the ventral striatum that I discussed earlier that is related
sentences.zh: 例如，我之前讨论过的腹侧纹状体的增加，这与

sentences.en: to reward value and feeling good are increasing during adolescence and at the same time brain regions involved in social perspective taking are increasing.
sentences.zh: 奖励价值和愉悦感有关，在青春期会增加，同时涉及社会视角采择的大脑区域也在增加。

sentences.en: And these together, I think, really promote the ability of adolescents to engage in really meaningful activities that bring them joy.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这些因素共同促进了青少年参与那些能给他们带来快乐的、真正有意义的活动的能力。

sentences.en: So, that reward sensitivity while also taking the perspective of others and thinking about the broader societal needs of their community.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种奖励敏感性与换位思考以及对社区更广泛社会需求的思考是并存的。

sentences.en: And so, we see that adolescents, as you mentioned, are engaging in really positive behaviors during this period.
sentences.zh: 正如您所提到的，我们看到青少年在这一时期确实在参与非常积极的行为。

sentences.en: They're leading social movements.
sentences.zh: 他们正在领导社会运动。

sentences.en: They're also doing this at a smaller scale, whether that be contributing to their family or helping their friends or volunteering at their local community.
sentences.zh: 他们也在小范围内这样做，无论是为家庭做贡献、帮助朋友，还是在当地社区做志愿者。

sentences.en: Some teens do this at such a huge level.
sentences.zh: 有些青少年在很大程度上做到了这一点。

sentences.en: So, leading the climate change movements, leading these bigger scale movements that have gotten tons and tons of people involved.
sentences.zh: 比如领导气候变化运动，领导那些吸引了成千上万人的大规模运动。

sentences.en: But it doesn't have to happen at that scale.
sentences.zh: 但这并不一定要达到那种规模。

sentences.en: And adolescents in their everyday lives are doing activities that are pro-social and community-oriented.
sentences.zh: 青少年在日常生活中也在从事亲社会和以社区为导向的活动。

sentences.en: And they're not doing this just to get into college, for example.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做不仅仅是为了考大学。

sentences.en: But there's research showing that these brain regions involved in reward sensitivity and social sensitivity are activated, suggesting that it really does bring
sentences.zh: 有研究表明，涉及奖励敏感性和社会敏感性的大脑区域被激活了，这表明参与这些活动确实能给

sentences.en: them joy to engage in this.
sentences.zh: 他们带来快乐。

sentences.en: And it is a meaningful activity for adolescents.
sentences.zh: 这对青少年来说是一项有意义的活动。

sentences.en: How does culture affect teens' experiences of adolescents?
sentences.zh: 文化如何影响青少年对青春期的体验？

sentences.en: Do teens in different countries show similar changes in behavior and brain development during the years that you study?
sentences.zh: 在您研究的这些年里，不同国家的青少年在行为和大脑发育方面表现出相似的变化吗？

sentences.en: In a way, adolescent is a social construction.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，青春期是一种社会建构。

sentences.en: And so, if the society that you live in determines how adolescence is viewed.
sentences.zh: 你所处的社会决定了青春期是如何被看待的。

sentences.en: So, the stereotypes of adolescents are determined by the culture we live in.
sentences.zh: 因此，对青少年的刻板印象是由我们所处的文化决定的。

sentences.en: In some cultures, adolescence is described as a time of risk-taking and this storm and stress, which was one of the very original ways of describing adolescence.
sentences.zh: 在某些文化中，青春期被描述为冒险和“狂风骤雨”的时期，这是描述青春期最初的方式之一。

sentences.en: And some cultures don't view it in that way.
sentences.zh: 而有些文化并不这样看待它。

sentences.en: And what's really interesting is that in the way that one's culture views adolescence, oftentimes adolescence is experienced in those ways.
sentences.zh: 非常有趣的是，一个人所处的文化如何看待青春期，往往也会以那种方式去体验青春期。

sentences.en: So, there has been cross-cultural research.
sentences.zh: 所以，确实有跨文化研究。

sentences.en: For example, Young Q, who's now an assistant professor at Northwestern, has done research in China and the
sentences.zh: 例如，现在西北大学担任助理教授的Young Q，就在中国和

sentences.en: United States to look at how these stereotypes of adolescents are different.
sentences.zh: 美国进行了研究，观察这些对青少年的刻板印象有何不同。

sentences.en: And they differ in China and they differ in the United States.
sentences.zh: 结果显示，中国和美国的情况确实存在差异。

sentences.en: And China adolescence is viewed less so at this time of risk-taking and peer influence and more so as this time of family obligation and educational motivation
sentences.zh: 在中国，青春期被视为一个较少涉及冒险和同伴影响的时期，而更多地被看作是一个承担家庭义务和追求学业动力的阶段

sentences.en: than, for example, in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 与美国相比，例如。

sentences.en: And so, there's definitely ways in which the culture that we live in can affect how adolescents are viewed.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们所处的文化确实在很大程度上影响了人们对青少年的看法。

sentences.en: And what's important to keep in mind is that these stereotypes and views of adolescents are often self-fulfilling prophecies.
sentences.zh: 需要记住的一点是，这些关于青少年的刻板印象和观点往往会成为自我实现的预言。

sentences.en: So, if I grow up in a culture that views adolescence as this time of risk-taking, I'm more likely to think that adolescence is a time of risk-taking
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我在一种将青春期视为冒险时期的文化中长大，我就更有可能认为青春期就是冒险的时期

sentences.en: and therefore engage in more risk-taking because I think that that's what adolescents are supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 并因此参与更多的冒险行为，因为我认为这就是青少年应该做的事情。

sentences.en: And so, there's definitely ways in which culture impacts just the mere experience of what adolescence
sentences.zh: 所以，文化确实在很大程度上影响了青春期本身的体验，

sentences.en: is described as, the stereotypes that are endorsed by that group, and how adolescents growing up in that culture might view and experience adolescence themselves.
sentences.zh: 包括对青春期的描述、该群体所认同的刻板印象，以及在那种文化中长大的青少年如何看待和体验自己的青春期。

sentences.en: What about differences between the sexes?
sentences.zh: 那么性别之间有什么差异吗？

sentences.en: A lot of people say that girls are more mature than boys, that they are more sensible than their male counterparts.
sentences.zh: 很多人说女孩比男孩更成熟，她们比同龄男孩更懂事。

sentences.en: Do girls take fewer risks or is this a groundless belief or do they take different types of risks?
sentences.zh: 女孩承担的风险更少吗？这是一种毫无根据的信念，还是她们承担的是不同类型的风险？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a great question that I don't have the full answer for, but the short answer just from our work is that we don't find gender differences.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题，我没有完整的答案，但从我们的工作来看，简短的回答是我们没有发现性别差异。

sentences.en: Boys and girls don't differ in the amount of risks they take.
sentences.zh: 男孩和女孩在承担风险的数量上没有区别。

sentences.en: I think we need more well-powered studies, and by that I mean large sample sizes that look at
sentences.zh: 我认为我们需要更多高质量的研究，我的意思是需要大样本量来研究

sentences.en: risk-taking across many different behaviors to get a better sense of whether girls and boys might differ in the types of risks that they take.
sentences.zh: 多种不同行为中的冒险倾向，以便更好地了解女孩和男孩在承担风险的类型上是否存在差异。

sentences.en: There are, in the literature out there, I'm less versed with it, so don't want to say too much, but there is some evidence that girls and boys might differ
sentences.zh: 在现有的文献中，我对此了解不多，所以不想说太多，但确实有一些证据表明女孩和男孩可能存在差异，

sentences.en: in terms of externalizing behaviors, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如在外部化行为方面。

sentences.en: But I think that girls and boys actually are more similar to each other than they are different, and that the variability is really within these groups of adolescents.
sentences.zh: 但我认为女孩和男孩实际上比他们之间的差异更相似，真正的变异性其实存在于这些青少年群体内部。

sentences.en: So it will range across girls as much as it'll range across boys.
sentences.zh: 所以女孩之间的差异范围和男孩之间的差异范围是一样的。

sentences.en: Do you know whether there are differences based on race and ethnicity or socioeconomic status?
sentences.zh: 你知道基于种族、民族或社会经济地位是否存在差异吗？

sentences.en: You know, you could imagine that somebody who is living in a tougher situation might be willing to take more risks because, you know, what do I have to lose here, right?
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，生活在更艰难环境中的人可能更愿意冒险，因为，你知道，我还能失去什么呢，对吧？

sentences.en: My life is already tough.
sentences.zh: 我的生活已经很艰难了。

sentences.en: Yes, there's definitely evidence, especially when it comes to socioeconomic status,
sentences.zh: 是的，确实有证据，特别是在社会经济地位方面，

sentences.en: that teens from lower SES environments are more likely to take risks and engage in externalizing behaviors for exactly the point you raised that, like, what is there to lose?
sentences.zh: 来自较低社会经济地位环境的青少年更有可能冒险并参与外部化行为，原因正是你提到的，反正也没什么可失去的。

sentences.en: Or actually, maybe there's something really to gain by engaging that's risk-taking.
sentences.zh: 或者实际上，通过参与这种冒险行为，可能真的能获得一些东西。

sentences.en: So if my family can't afford to put food on the table, I might go out and steal or engage in other behaviors in order to help my family.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我的家庭负担不起伙食费，我可能会出去偷窃或从事其他行为来帮助我的家庭。

sentences.en: And that's considered a huge risk.
sentences.zh: 这被认为是一种巨大的风险。

sentences.en: But it may actually be in the end, the outcome is helpful for them and their family.
sentences.zh: 但最终，其结果对他们和他们的家庭来说可能是有帮助的。

sentences.en: Or being exposed to an environment that has lots of risks and negative experiences in the environment, whether you're growing up in a place with a lot of violence or
sentences.zh: 或者暴露在一个充满风险和负面经历的环境中，无论你是在一个充满暴力的地方长大，还是

sentences.en: being exposed to other things.
sentences.zh: 暴露在其他事物中。

sentences.en: There's instances where either taking a risk is a good thing, or taking a risk is something that is socialized within that environment, because of what you're exposed to.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，冒险可能是一件好事，或者由于你所处的环境，冒险是被该环境所社会化的行为。

sentences.en: When it comes to SES or ethnic racial differences, the literature is much more mixed.
sentences.zh: 当谈到社会经济地位或种族差异时，文献的结论要复杂得多。

sentences.en: And so there's not kind of clear differences there.
sentences.zh: 所以这方面并没有明确的差异。

sentences.en: I think, again, similar to boys and girls, there's more similarities than there are differences.
sentences.zh: 我认为，同样地，就像男孩和女孩一样，相似之处多于差异。

sentences.en: And the differences are not at all due to anything that's like biologically wired, that's different between racial or ethnic
sentences.zh: 而且这些差异绝不是由于种族或民族群体之间在生物学上的任何差异所致，

sentences.en: groups, but perhaps something that is culturally socialized, if there are differences that are found.
sentences.zh: 如果确实发现了差异，那可能是一些文化社会化的结果。

sentences.en: In our culture, we have kind of prolonged adolescence.
sentences.zh: 在我们的文化中，我们有一种延长的青春期。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, we've, kids are living with their parents longer for economic and for other reasons.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，孩子们因为经济和其他原因与父母住在一起的时间更长了。

sentences.en: You know, we're really sort of, in a sense, you might say, you know, we've been coddling our kids.
sentences.zh: 你知道，从某种意义上说，你可以说我们一直在溺爱我们的孩子。

sentences.en: Is that having an impact on their desire to take risks there and risks that might be good for them?
sentences.zh: 这是否影响了他们冒险的欲望，以及那些可能对他们有益的风险？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So in either societies where kids have to grow up sooner or for other reasons where you
sentences.zh: 所以在那些孩子们必须更早成长的社会，或者由于其他原因，你

sentences.en: might have to grow up sooner, for example, if you don't have lots of resources or parents who are available.
sentences.zh: 可能不得不更早成长，例如，如果你没有足够的资源或没有可依靠的父母。

sentences.en: And for example, if you're in the foster system and don't have a mom and dad necessarily to support you well past 18, you might have to grow up sooner.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你在寄养系统中，没有妈妈和爸爸在18岁以后支持你，你可能不得不更早成长。

sentences.en: Whereas for teens in higher SDS environments, or for those who do have parents who one can live with for longer past the high school
sentences.zh: 而对于处于较高社会经济地位环境的青少年，或者那些有父母可以让他们在高中毕业后继续居住的人来说，

sentences.en: years, when you're technically defined by society to be an adult, this provides an opportunity to kind of grow up slower.
sentences.zh: 当你从社会定义上成为成年人时，这提供了一个慢慢成长的机会。

sentences.en: In a lot of ways, this can be positive.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，这可能是积极的。

sentences.en: There's research from both animal models and actually human models showing that the brain slows down in development when given the
sentences.zh: 来自动物模型和人类模型的研究表明，当给予机会时，大脑的发育会放缓，

sentences.en: opportunity to, but speeds up and becomes more mature sooner in environments where you kind of have to grow up sooner.
sentences.zh: 但在必须更早成长的环境中，大脑发育会加速并更早成熟。

sentences.en: And both are adaptive.
sentences.zh: 两者都是适应性的。

sentences.en: You're adapting to the environment to which you need to either grow up sooner or have more opportunity to explore your environment.
sentences.zh: 你正在适应你需要更早成长或有更多机会探索环境的环境。

sentences.en: And so by prolonging adolescence, we're giving teens the opportunity to explore more, explore their identity, explore
sentences.zh: 因此，通过延长青春期，我们给了青少年更多的机会去探索，探索他们的身份，探索

sentences.en: different opportunities for like who they want to be when they grow up, engage in different types of risk that might be very adaptive for reaching those goals.
sentences.zh: 各种不同的机会，比如他们长大后想成为什么样的人，参与不同类型的风险，这些可能对实现这些目标非常有帮助。

sentences.en: And so if you're in an environment that allows you to kind of slow down that process of developing and growing up, then it's perhaps a positive thing
sentences.zh: 所以如果你处于一个允许你放慢发展和成长过程的环境中，那么这可能对年轻人来说是一件积极的事情，

sentences.en: for youth and not something that we necessarily need to look down on.
sentences.zh: 而不是我们必须看不起的事情。

sentences.en: Like they're just not growing up and they're staying teenagers forever and they're not getting married and having kids until later.
sentences.zh: 比如他们只是没有长大，他们永远是青少年，直到很晚才结婚生子。

sentences.en: Maybe this is a positive thing that allows them to really explore and define who they are and make decisions that are going to be the best for them as they reach adulthood.
sentences.zh: 也许这是一件积极的事情，让他们真正探索并定义自己，并在进入成年期时做出最适合他们的决定。

sentences.en: Now, you also study teens and technology and social media use.
sentences.zh: 现在，你也研究青少年与科技及社交媒体的使用。

sentences.en: And I know you're interested not only in how it's affecting their social and emotional lives, but how it might be shaping their brain development.
sentences.zh: 我知道你不仅对它如何影响他们的社交和情感生活感兴趣，还对它如何塑造他们的大脑发育感兴趣。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: What are the questions you're trying to answer by looking at this particular situation?
sentences.zh: 通过观察这个特殊的情况，你试图回答的问题是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So social media has really, I think, changed the social landscape of what adolescence looks like
sentences.zh: 我认为社交媒体确实改变了当今青春期的社交格局，

sentences.en: today compared to, for example, when I was a teenager and had to see my peers either in person or talk to them on the phone in order to interact with them.
sentences.zh: 与我十几岁时相比，那时我必须亲自见到同龄人或通过电话与他们交谈才能进行互动。

sentences.en: There's this around the clock ability to engage either synchronously or asynchronously.
sentences.zh: 现在有一种全天候的同步或异步参与能力。

sentences.en: And by that, I mean, you can be texting back and forth into the wee hours of the night.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以一直发短信到深夜。

sentences.en: You can be scrolling through social media and putting up comments and getting likes and getting feedback on that very quickly.
sentences.zh: 你可以滚动浏览社交媒体，发表评论，获得点赞，并非常迅速地得到反馈。

sentences.en: And this, we think, has really changed what it means to be an adolescent, what peer relationships might look like, teens' ability to connect with others, their sense of loneliness.
sentences.zh: 我们认为，这确实改变了作为青少年的意义，同伴关系的样子，青少年与他人联系的能力，以及他们的孤独感。

sentences.en: And this is happening in both good and bad ways.
sentences.zh: 这种情况正在以好坏两方面发生。

sentences.en: And so we're trying to unpack what that means in terms of how they're able to stay connected to others, to find others who might share their similar interests.
sentences.zh: 所以我们试图解析这意味着什么，包括他们如何能够与他人保持联系，找到可能与他们有相似兴趣的人。

sentences.en: And ways that this may be increasing their sense of loneliness or negative aspects in their body image.
sentences.zh: 以及这可能增加他们的孤独感或对身体形象产生负面影响的方式。

sentences.en: The exciting piece that we're starting to explore, which we don't have data to share yet, is how this might be co-occurring with their brain development.
sentences.zh: 我们开始探索的一个令人兴奋的部分是，这可能如何与他们的大脑发育同时发生，尽管我们还没有数据可以分享。

sentences.en: So we know that the adolescent brain is highly sensitive to rewards.
sentences.zh: 我们知道青少年大脑对奖励高度敏感。

sentences.en: It's highly sensitive to social feedback.
sentences.zh: 它对社交反馈高度敏感。

sentences.en: And so how might this interact with the ways that they're engaging in these online platforms in social media and digital media contexts?
sentences.zh: 那么这可能如何与他们在这些在线平台、社交媒体和数字媒体环境中的参与方式相互作用呢？

sentences.en: And does the brain then get shaped by those experiences?
sentences.zh: 大脑是否会因此被这些经历所塑造？

sentences.en: Because the brain itself is highly plastic and sensitive to its environment.
sentences.zh: 因为大脑本身具有高度的可塑性，并且对环境敏感。

sentences.en: The adolescent period is a huge time of brain development, second only to that that we see in infancy.
sentences.zh: 青春期是一个大脑发育的重要时期，仅次于婴儿期。

sentences.en: And so not only do we see this heightened sensitivity in terms of reward sensitivity and
sentences.zh: 所以我们不仅看到了在奖励敏感性和

sentences.en: social sensitivity, but we see that the environment and things that teens are exposed to can shape further brain development.
sentences.zh: 社交敏感性方面的这种高度敏感，而且我们看到环境和青少年所接触的事物可以进一步塑造大脑发育。

sentences.en: And so we don't yet know how these digital media platforms and what they're experiencing online might be integrated into their brains.
sentences.zh: 所以我们还不知道这些数字媒体平台以及他们在网上经历的事情是如何整合到他们的大脑中的。

sentences.en: So that's something that we're just very interested in exploring and are starting to conduct longitudinal research to follow teens across
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们非常有兴趣探索的事情，并且已经开始进行纵向研究，以跟踪青少年随时间的变化，

sentences.en: time and understand the bi-directional relationships here.
sentences.zh: 并了解其中的双向关系。

sentences.en: So how is adolescents' neurobiological sensitivity affecting maybe how they engage online and vice versa?
sentences.zh: 那么青少年的神经生物学敏感性是如何影响他们在线参与方式的，反之亦然？

sentences.en: How is the way that they engage on these digital platforms shaping potential changes in brain development across time?
sentences.zh: 他们在这些数字平台上的参与方式如何随着时间的推移塑造大脑发育的潜在变化？

sentences.en: I thought it was really interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常有趣。

sentences.en: And there was a recent Forbes article about your technology research and Jim Winston, whose foundation funds the center at UNC that you had.
sentences.zh: 最近有一篇关于你的科技研究的《福布斯》文章，吉姆·温斯顿（Jim Winston），他的基金会资助了你在北卡罗来纳大学的中心，

sentences.en: He said, a child born today and primarily raised on devices will be neurobiologically incapable of reading war and peace as an adult, not lazy or unmotivated, incapable.
sentences.zh: 他说，一个今天出生并主要在设备上长大的孩子，成年后将在神经生物学上无法阅读《战争与和平》，不是因为懒惰或缺乏动力，而是因为无法做到。

sentences.en: Do you agree with that?
sentences.zh: 你同意这一点吗？

sentences.en: I mean, do we even know whether that's the case?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们甚至知道情况是否如此吗？

sentences.en: I don't think we know.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们知道。

sentences.en: We definitely need empirical research that follows youth from childhood to adolescence into adulthood to be able to answer that question.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对需要实证研究来跟踪年轻人从童年到青春期再到成年，才能回答这个问题。

sentences.en: We really don't have the data yet to even know how their use of digital media is impacting brain development and their ability to do things like reading war and peace.
sentences.zh: 我们确实还没有数据来了解他们对数字媒体的使用如何影响大脑发育以及他们阅读《战争与和平》等事情的能力。

sentences.en: And so we're just not there yet.
sentences.zh: 所以我们还没有达到那个阶段。

sentences.en: We need much more research to be able to support those types of comments.
sentences.zh: 我们需要更多的研究来支持这类评论。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what we're trying to do with our longitudinal research is to be able to understand these mechanisms and how digital media might shape brain development.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们试图通过纵向研究来做的事情，即了解这些机制以及数字媒体如何塑造大脑发育。

sentences.en: And of course, vice versa for both good and bad ways.
sentences.zh: 当然，反之亦然，无论是好是坏。

sentences.en: We don't know the positive and negative ways that this could be occurring because like I said,
sentences.zh: 我们不知道这可能发生的积极和消极方式，因为正如我所说，

sentences.en: with the growing up too fast versus maturing more early, how that impacts brain development.
sentences.zh: 就像成长过快与过早成熟一样，这如何影响大脑发育。

sentences.en: It's the same thing with digital media.
sentences.zh: 数字媒体也是一样。

sentences.en: The brain is adapting to its environment.
sentences.zh: 大脑正在适应其环境。

sentences.en: And so in a way, whatever the brain is doing to respond to these social inputs is adaptive.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，大脑为响应这些社交输入所做的任何事情都是适应性的。

sentences.en: Whether we qualify that as a good thing or bad thing is subjective, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为，我们将此定性为好事还是坏事是主观的。

sentences.en: And so understanding these processes is going to take a lot of time because we need to do longitudinal research.
sentences.zh: 因此，理解这些过程需要很长时间，因为我们需要进行纵向研究。

sentences.en: And also we need to take into context whether this is a good thing or bad thing, because much of it is subjective based on what we think adolescents should be doing
sentences.zh: 而且我们还需要考虑这是否是一件好事或坏事，因为其中很多是主观的，基于我们认为青少年应该做什么，

sentences.en: or how we think these outcomes are impacting their development.
sentences.zh: 或者我们认为这些结果如何影响他们的发展。

sentences.en: Any other big questions that you're trying to answer at this point?
sentences.zh: 目前你还在试图回答其他什么重大问题吗？

sentences.en: I think that our main research is really just trying to unpack and answer a lot of the potential stereotypes that are out there.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们的主要研究实际上只是试图解析和回答现有的许多潜在刻板印象。

sentences.en: So we have work happening right now looking at peer influence.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在正在进行关于同伴影响的研究。

sentences.en: So we talked about this earlier, but also really considering the positive side of peer influence is one of our big goals.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈到了这一点，但真正考虑同伴影响的积极面也是我们的主要目标之一。

sentences.en: There is just as much evidence suggesting that peers can push teens to engage in very good
sentences.zh: 有同样多的证据表明同伴可以推动青少年参与非常好的

sentences.en: behaviors and change their attitudes in more positive ways as there is evidence on the contrary that peers drive teens to be more risky.
sentences.zh: 行为并以更积极的方式改变他们的态度，正如相反的证据表明同伴驱使青少年变得更冒险一样。

sentences.en: And so this is a big area of research that we're eager to contribute to more and kind of debunk if we can with empirical evidence, this idea that teens are driving each
sentences.zh: 这是一个我们渴望做出更多贡献的研究领域，并尽可能用实证证据来揭穿这种观点，即青少年在驱使彼此

sentences.en: other to engage in more negative and deviant behaviors, but actually are promoting very positive behaviors as well.
sentences.zh: 参与更多消极和越轨的行为，而实际上他们也在促进非常积极的行为。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Telzer, this has been very interesting.
sentences.zh: 好的，泰尔泽博士，这非常有趣。

sentences.en: I really appreciate your joining me today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你今天加入我。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: You can read more about Dr. Telzer's research and other research on the teenage brain in the July-August issue of APA's magazine, Monitor on Psychology.
sentences.zh: 你可以在美国心理学会杂志《心理学监测》（Monitor on Psychology）的7月-8月刊中阅读更多关于泰尔泽博士的研究以及其他关于青少年大脑的研究。

sentences.en: You'll find a link on our website at www.speakingofpsychology.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 上找到链接。

sentences.en: You can also find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology there or on Apple, Stitcher, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你也可以在那里或在 Apple、Stitcher 或任何你获取播客的地方找到《心理学谈话》（Speaking of Psychology）之前的剧集。

sentences.en: And if you like what you hear, please leave us a review.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢你所听到的，请给我们留下评论。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的播客有意见或想法，可以通过 speakingofpsychology@apa.org 给我们发电子邮件。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》由李·温纳曼（Lee Weinerman）制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Condayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的声音编辑是克里斯·康达扬（Chris Condayan）。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 代表美国心理学会，我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。
